Get started

Set up GitHub, choose your agent features, and open your first repository.

About ByteQuay

ByteQuay is a macOS app for GitHub reviews and local coding agents. Let agents build and guide you, choose how much detail to explore, and merge when you feel confident.

A workspace holds a repository’s work. A task is an agent conversation with its own working copy. App data stays on your Mac; GitHub and model requests use the services you connect.

ByteQuay is pre-1.0. These guides cover the development version; check your release notes for availability.

Get started

  1. Download ByteQuay from GitHub Releases. Open the DMG and drag the app to Applications. Follow your release’s requirements; current builds need macOS 14+ and include Java 25, so no separate JDK installation is required.
  2. Follow the setup guide to choose your appearance, connect GitHub, and decide which agent features to use. You can continue without an agent.
  3. Choose Home → Repos you watch → + Watch. Select a repository, check its branch and publication destinations, then Watch repository.
  4. Open Pull requests, select a PR, and inspect WorkBench → Changes.

Choose your setup

  1. Appearance and GitHub: choose System, Light, or Dark. Connect with Use my GitHub CLI login after running gh auth login, or Connect with token →. The app recommends a classic token with repo and read:user scopes.
  2. Connect an agent and choose your default: check Codex or Claude Code, sign in, or add a DeepSeek API key. Select the account and model for Development; Review follows it unless you choose another in Settings.
  3. Automation: choose how far new tasks go on their own, from a local commit to a merged PR. It starts at Auto-Commit on a fresh installation. Existing preferences are preserved.
  4. Your features: watch the previews to explore Today and Assistant, then enable either feature if you want it. Each uses your default Development agent and model allowance. Assistant task actions have separate switches.

After GitHub is connected, Continue without an agent keeps GitHub and PR work available. If an agent is already available, Skip remaining setup keeps the remaining saved choices. New agent actions stay hidden until their selected agent and model are usable; saved tasks, reviews, and notices remain.

Unfinished setup resumes where you left it. Once completed, it never opens automatically again, including after a sign-in expires. To revisit it, choose Settings → General → Setup guide → Open setup. You can also connect a provider or change Settings → Personal → Appearance directly.

Home and workspaces

Home brings together watched repositories and recent activity. A workspace holds tasks, PRs, work items, commits, and memory.

  • Choose Direct clone to work in the selected repository, or Personal fork to publish through your fork. Review the source, push, and PR destinations before confirming.
  • My PRs shows your open work. Snooze hides a card temporarily; Needs attention shows up to five updates needing a response.
  • Approved by me initially shows up to three open PRs you approved on Home and workspace Home, newest activity first, even after reading them. Choose Show all to see the rest or Show less to return to three. Pushes, comments, and check updates stay there without returning to Needs attention. A new review request or dismissed approval brings the PR back for review. Merged and closed PRs leave this section.
  • Unwatch retires a workspace while keeping local history. Watch again restores it. Delete local data is a separate, confirmed removal.

Plan the day with Today

Today is off until you enable it during setup or in Settings → Agents → Features. It needs a usable global Development model, and each day’s list spends a model session from that account. Once on, Home opens on working days, after the time you set, with Today: up to five things worth doing first, each with a reason. An agent picks them from ByteQuay’s records; it never writes to GitHub or starts a task. If ByteQuay was closed at that time, Today is made when you return.

  • Click a row to open its PR, task, issue, ticket, or work item. Hover it for Done or Not today; a row also closes when its work happens.
  • The circular arrow makes the list again. A workspace Home shows only its repository’s rows; Needs attention marks Today rows with a sun.
  • On the last working day, This week looks back at what merged and slipped.
  • Settings → Agents → Features sets the time and working days, and can plan around your calendar’s busy times (never event titles).
